title: Client authentication bypass when client and server connections share a session store
summary: DTLS 1.2 resumption did not distinguish client-created from server-created sessions in a shared SessionStore. A malicious server previously contacted by the application must retain the session secret and reach its listener; it can resume the outbound session, after which the listener accepts application data without its usual PSK or client-certificate checks. The advisory says WebRTC users are unaffected.
ai_role: The Pion maintainer's case-specific advisory credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-ALO2G36N). It does not identify model versions or internal discovery dates.
classification_note: The cited advisory documents public disclosure; it does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory identifies fix commit 2b234cd and the following package-version scope: v2 2.1.0–2.2.12 (no patched v2 version listed); v3 before 3.1.14, fixed 3.1.14. This source does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: authentication bypass affecting listener application-data access under the stated shared-store and prior-outbound-contact conditions.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible attack path but does not report observed exploitation.
